## Why This Replaced the 14:36 Guarded Run

The earlier run `v5_zero_l6_guarded_20260703_1436` was a valid early health
run, but it used `train_v5.py` before fixed-environment metadata and
`env_version=v55` were wired in. That meant the run could not prove the final
V5 contract:

- fixed 200bb action-history / raise-cap environment
- explicit Slumbot observation encoder metadata
- checkpoint metadata proving actual-hand accounting and stack depth

It was stopped at early scale and marked:

`models/alpha_holdem_v5_from_zero/v5_zero_l6_guarded_20260703_1436/SUPERSEDED_LEGACY_ENVIRONMENT.txt`

## Post-1500 Throughput Audit

Checked at 2026-07-04 04:16 EDT while the active process was still running.

Evidence from `latest_train.log`:

- iterations 1-99: average `h/s=1,522.3`, average `inf_bs=22.3`,
  average `collect=10.9s`
- iterations 100-199: average `h/s=1,445.3`, average `inf_bs=22.6`,
  average `collect=11.4s`
- iterations 200-599: average `h/s=797.6`, average `inf_bs=11.2`,
  average `collect=21.6s`
- iterations 600-999: average `h/s=474.6`, average `inf_bs=6.4`,
  average `collect=34.9s`
- iterations 1000-1506: average `h/s=424.1`, average `inf_bs=5.1`,
  average `collect=39.2s`

Diagnosis:

Once the opponent pool fills, the original per-worker opponent sampler splits
28 rollout workers across self-play plus up to five pool snapshots. That keeps
the long-run K-best mix, but it fragments GPU inference into small model groups;
the observed average inference batch drops from about 22 to about 5. PPO update
time is only about 2-3 seconds per iteration, so the run is rollout/inference
pipeline bound, not PPO-update bound.

Future-run trainer adjustment:

- `train_v5.py` now supports `--opponent-assignment per-iteration|per-worker`
- default for future launches/restarts is `per-iteration`
- `per-iteration` samples either self-play or one pool snapshot for the whole
  rollout iteration, preserving the long-run self-play/pool distribution while
  keeping inference batches large
- `per-worker` preserves the original independent sampler for ablation

Verification:

```bash
python -m py_compile scripts/alpha_holdem/train_v5.py
python -X utf8 -u scripts/alpha_holdem/train_v5.py --device cpu --workers 2 --hands-per-iter 4 --total-hands 4 --ppo-epochs 1 --mini-batch-size 4 --snapshot-every 1 --save-interval 1 --run-dir tmp/v5_assignment_smoke --run-id assignment --overwrite --max-runtime-seconds 120 --opponent-assignment per-iteration
```

Result:

- syntax check passed
- CPU smoke completed
- smoke checkpoint saved at `tmp/v5_assignment_smoke/latest.pt`
- smoke manifest/config includes `opponent_assignment=per-iteration`

Important limitation:

The active training process was already running and has not been stopped, so
this throughput change is not active in PID 39172. It will only affect a
controlled restart/new launch. No Slumbot, L5, or L6 claim is allowed from this
engineering change alone.

## Continuation Metadata and Gate Rule

Checked at 2026-07-04 04:23 EDT.

Problem:

To apply the throughput fix without throwing away valid V5-from-zero training,
we need to be able to restart from a V5 checkpoint. The old gate rule implicitly
treated `resume=None` as proof of a from-zero run. That is too strict for normal
checkpoint continuation and too weak as a long-term lineage rule.

Trainer/verifier adjustment:

- `train_v5.py` now writes `resume`, `fresh_from_zero_lineage`,
  `lineage_root_run_id`, and `lineage_parent_checkpoint` into checkpoints and
  manifests
- fresh random-init V5 launches write `fresh_from_zero_lineage=True`
- continuation from a V5-from-zero checkpoint preserves
  `fresh_from_zero_lineage=True` while truthfully recording the resume path
- `v5_gate_watch.py` now checks `fresh_from_zero_lineage=True` instead of
  requiring `resume=None`
- old fresh V5 checkpoints without the new field are treated as from-zero only
  when `version=v5.zero` and no resume source was recorded

Verification:

```bash
python -m py_compile scripts/alpha_holdem/train_v5.py scripts/alpha_holdem/v5_gate_watch.py
python -X utf8 -u scripts/alpha_holdem/train_v5.py --device cpu --workers 2 --hands-per-iter 4 --total-hands 4 --ppo-epochs 1 --mini-batch-size 4 --snapshot-every 1 --save-interval 1 --run-dir tmp/v5_lineage_fresh --run-id lineage_fresh --overwrite --max-runtime-seconds 120 --opponent-assignment per-iteration
python -X utf8 -u scripts/alpha_holdem/train_v5.py --device cpu --workers 2 --hands-per-iter 4 --total-hands 60 --ppo-epochs 1 --mini-batch-size 4 --snapshot-every 1 --save-interval 1 --run-dir tmp/v5_lineage_continue --run-id lineage_continue --resume tmp/v5_lineage_fresh/latest.pt --allow-resume --no-reset-optimizer --max-runtime-seconds 120 --opponent-assignment per-iteration
python scripts/alpha_holdem/v5_monitor.py --run-dir tmp/v5_lineage_continue --min-hps-warn 0 --allin-warn 1 --allin-fail 1 --mix-dominance-warn 1 --mix-dominance-fail 1
python -u scripts/alpha_holdem/v5_gate_watch.py --run-dir tmp/v5_lineage_continue --target-iteration 2 --expected-pool-snapshots 2 --poll-seconds 1 --timeout-seconds 0
```

Result:

- fresh smoke saved a V5 checkpoint with `fresh_from_zero_lineage=True`
- continuation smoke resumed that checkpoint with optimizer state preserved
- continuation checkpoint recorded
  `resume=tmp\v5_lineage_fresh\latest.pt`
- continuation checkpoint preserved `fresh_from_zero_lineage=True`
- gate verifier returned PASS for the continuation checkpoint

Operational implication:

A future controlled restart to activate `--opponent-assignment per-iteration`
should use checkpoint continuation, not a new external baseline:

```bash
python -X utf8 -u scripts/alpha_holdem/train_v5.py --device cuda --workers 28 --hands-per-iter 16384 --total-hands 2700000000 --starting-stack 200 --env-version v55 --lr 3e-4 --gamma 0.999 --delta1 3.0 --entropy-coef 0.05 --entropy-floor 0.3 --k-best 5 --self-play-fraction 0.2 --opponent-assignment per-iteration --snapshot-every 200 --save-interval 100 --resume models/alpha_holdem_v5_from_zero/v5_zero_l6_fixedenv_20260703_1445/latest.pt --allow-resume --no-reset-optimizer --run-id <continuation-run-id> --run-dir <continuation-run-dir>
```

The active PID 39172 has not been restarted. This section only prepares the
metadata and gate rules needed for a later controlled restart decision.

## Post-Gate Continuation Automation

Checked at 2026-07-04 04:27 EDT.

Added `scripts/alpha_holdem/v5_continue_after_gate.ps1`.

Purpose:

- verify a source V5 gate before any continuation launch
- verify checkpoint metadata and V5-from-zero lineage
- generate the continuation command with `--opponent-assignment per-iteration`
- refuse to launch if the source trainer is still alive unless
  `-StopOldTraining` is explicitly provided
- optionally start the next gate watcher after launch


- PowerShell parser check passed

- active checkpoint fallback lineage was accepted because it has
  `version=v5.zero` and `resume=None`

  `--resume <active latest.pt> --allow-resume --no-reset-optimizer
  --opponent-assignment per-iteration`

No process was stopped and no continuation trainer was launched.

## Slumbot Handoff Audit - 2026-07-04 10:11 EDT

The Slumbot benchmark handoff tooling was rechecked while the trainer waited
for gate 2500.

Verified chain:

- `v5_slumbot_plan_watch.py` is read-only. It refreshes benchmark plan
  JSON/Markdown and exits only when the selected stage is READY or
  READY_WITH_WARNINGS; it does not call Slumbot.
- `v5_slumbot_benchmark_plan.py` has three staged gates:
  - `quick5k`: 5,000 planned hands, minimum 50M training hands, smoke only.
  - `promotion20k`: 20,400 planned hands by default, minimum 250M training
    hands, promotion screen only.
  - `formal100k`: 100,000 planned hands by default, minimum 250M training
    hands, only this stage can produce L5/L6-eligible evidence if CI passes.
- `bench_v55_slumbot.ps1` runs the actual sessions and writes per-session
  result JSON plus per-hand JSONL, then runs CI and promotion-gate summaries.
- `slumbot_ci_from_hands.py` computes bb/100 and 95% CI from saved per-hand
  JSONL records. Its formal L5 condition is exactly:
  `hands >= 100000`, `bb/100 > 0`, and `lower_bound_bb_per_100 > 0`.
- `v5_slumbot_promotion_gate.py` rechecks checkpoint metadata, health,
  hand-artifact presence, stack depth, fresh-from-zero lineage, and CI before
  allowing any promotion/L5/L6 decision.

No patch was made in this audit because the existing chain already blocks the
two main failure modes:

- a quick 5k smoke result cannot be promoted to L5/L6;
- a 20k promotion result cannot be used as a formal Slumbot win claim.

Current status remains unchanged: no Slumbot benchmark has been run for this
V5 line, and no L5/L6 claim is supported yet.

## Scorecard Evidence-Gating Fix - 2026-07-04 15:50 EDT

The scorecard previously allowed 1k diagnostic Slumbot CI artifacts to influence the displayed Slumbot `overall` level.
That made the run look like `L1` because the greedy 1k diagnostic had the best lower bound among all artifacts,
even though the only non-diagnostic Slumbot evidence was the 5k quick benchmark at `L0`.

Fix applied:

- `diagnostic`: `< 5,000` Slumbot hands; tracked but excluded from official Slumbot level and trend claims.
- `smoke`: `5,000` to `< 20,400` hands; useful evidence, not enough for baseline/promotion claims.
- `promotion`: `20,400` to `< 100,000` hands; can screen against the V4/BC baseline.
- `formal`: `100,000+` hands; required for L5/L6 claims.

Current corrected scorecard:

- official Slumbot overall: `L0`
- latest non-diagnostic evidence: quick5k, `5,000` hands, `-76.221 bb/100`
- latest diagnostic evidence: greedy-guarded 1k, `-46.664 bb/100`
- L5/L6 claims remain blocked.

## Loss-KBest Pool Strategy Patch - 2026-07-04 16:38 EDT

The active GPU process is still using the strategy it loaded at launch, but
future V5 launches/restarts now support a closer K-best-style pool instead of
plain FIFO latest-K.

Change:

- `train_v5.py` now supports `--pool-strategy latest|loss-kbest`.
- default is `loss-kbest`.
- each snapshot records `selection_loss`, `selection_score`, and score components.
- `loss-kbest` keeps the K snapshots with the lowest Trinal-Clip selection-loss proxy:
  `policy_loss + 0.5*log1p(value_loss)`.
- checkpoint metadata now records `pool_strategy`, `pool_active_metadata`, and
  metadata-only `pool_candidate_history`.
- `v5_gate_watch.py` and `v5_gate_sequence_watch.py` can require
  `--expected-pool-strategy loss-kbest`.
- continuation/cutover scripts now pass `--pool-strategy loss-kbest` explicitly.

Why:

- The paper's K-best method selects historical survivors by ELO.
- The previous active trainer used latest-K FIFO, which can preserve recency but
  cannot claim K-best selection.
- Full ELO tournaments are still a future upgrade; this patch is a single-GPU
  approximation using the Trinal-Clip loss signal, and must be validated by
  internal probes and Slumbot evidence.

Validation:

- `python -m py_compile scripts\alpha_holdem\train_v5.py scripts\alpha_holdem\v5_gate_watch.py scripts\alpha_holdem\v5_gate_sequence_watch.py scripts\alpha_holdem\v5_throughput_sweep_plan.py`
- PowerShell parser check passed for:
  - `scripts\alpha_holdem\v5_continue_after_gate.ps1`
  - `scripts\alpha_holdem\v5_post_gate_execute_watch.ps1`
- CPU smoke: `tmp\v5_loss_kbest_smoke_20260704_163730`
  - final iteration: `4`
  - pool strategy: `loss-kbest`
  - K: `2`
  - active pool ids: `[0, 2]`
  - candidate history selected flags: `[true, true, true, false]`
  - result confirms the fourth snapshot was rejected by score, not retained by FIFO.
- Gate check on the smoke run:
  - `pool_strategy`: PASS, `pool_strategy=loss-kbest`
  - `pool_snapshots`: PASS, `pool snapshots 2 >= 2`
- Cutover dry-run against the active run produced a continuation command with
  `--pool-strategy loss-kbest --pool-history-limit 200`, detected source trainer
  PID `42788`, and launched no process.
- Cutover tooling was extended so a new continuation run can also start:
  - dashboard watcher
  - eval cadence watcher
  - internal strength watcher
  - checkpoint archive watcher
- A follow-up dry-run confirmed the recommended guarded cutover command includes
  `-StartDashboardWatcher`, `-StartEvalCadenceWatcher`,
  `-StartInternalStrengthWatcher`, and `-StartCheckpointArchiveWatcher`.

Operational consequence:

- This patch is not hot-applied to PID `42788`.
- The current Slumbot/V4 status remains unchanged: V5 is still L0 and not proven
  stronger than V4.
- The next serious restart/fresh V5 run should require `pool_strategy=loss-kbest`
  at gates; pool size alone is no longer sufficient evidence of AlphaHoldem-style
  K-best training.
